faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Who can use the herbal dosage calculator?
faq.a1: The calculator is for adults aged 18 and older. HerbAlly does not calculate herbal doses for children or adolescents because botanical extract concentrations are not validated for pediatric dosing. Consult a qualified pediatric healthcare professional instead.
faq.q2: What is Clark's rule vs Young's rule?
faq.a2: Both are reference methods. Clark's rule scales by weight (weight in kg / 68 × adult dose). Young's rule scales by age (age / (age + 12) × adult dose). HerbAlly shows both so you can compare, and caps the result at the adult reference dose.
faq.q3: Is the herbal dosage calculator free?
faq.a3: Yes — free, no account required. Reference doses come from published clinical monographs (EMA HMPC, Health Canada, WHO, NCCIH, and PubMed) for herbs with an established adult oral dose; high-risk or toxic plants do not display a dose calculator.

Herbal products vary widely in concentration and are not validated for dosing in children or adolescents. Please speak with a qualified pediatric healthcare professional (for example, a paediatrician, pharmacist or the child's doctor) before giving any herbal product to a person under {age}.
calculatorForm.ageRequiredForAdultDose: Enter the patient's age before calculating. HerbAlly only calculates doses for people aged {age} or older, and it must be able to confirm that age.
calculatorForm.pediatricDoseBlockedRationale: Why this limit exists: the classic pediatric formulas (Clark's, Young's, Fried's) were designed to scale prescription-drug doses and have never been validated for herbal extracts. HerbAlly therefore does not show a number for minors rather than present an unverified pediatric dose that could be mistaken for medical advice.

explanations.clark: Based on Clark's Rule using a weight of {weight} kg. The standard adult reference weight is 68 kg (150 lb).
explanations.young: Based on Young's Rule using an age of {age} years. This is an age-based estimate and is less precise than weight-based methods.
explanations.bsa: Based on the body-surface-area method using a BSA of {bsa} m² (height {height} cm, weight {weight} kg). The standard adult BSA is 1.73 m².
explanations.fried: Based on Fried's Rule using an age of {months} months. It does not apply to adults 18 or over.

npnCheckerPage.heading: Health Canada NPN Supplement Decoder
npnCheckerPage.intro: Enter the 8-digit Natural Product Number (NPN) or DIN-HM printed on a supplement bottle sold in Canada to fetch Health Canada's official LNHPD licence, medicinal ingredients, cautions, and drug interaction matches.
npnCheckerPage.explainerBody1: Natural health products sold legally in Canada carry an 8-digit NPN (or DIN-HM for homeopathic remedies). HerbAlly queries Health Canada's official public Licensed Natural Health Products Database (LNHPD) live without storing personal medication searches.
npnCheckerPage.explainerBody2: Whenever a licensed medicinal ingredient is a botanical tracked in HerbAlly, you can jump straight to its full clinical monograph or screen every botanical ingredient in the bottle against your prescriptions.
